title: Derived scalar extension of locally finite free module sheaves
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Work with sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $M$ be an $R$-module sheaf such that every object of the site has a covering on each member $U$ of which $M|_U\cong R|_U^{\oplus r_U}$ for a finite integer $r_U\geq0$, using slice restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Then $M$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and the complex $M[0]$ concentrated in degree zero is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For every morphism $\varphi:R\to B$ of sheaves of commutative rings on the same site, the canonical comparison is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$:
$$B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}(B\otimes_R M)[0].$$
Use derived extension of scalars as in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] and ordinary scalar extension as in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The $B$-module sheaf $B\otimes_R M$ is locally finite free with the same local ranks, and the comparison is natural in $M$. No flatness of $B$ over $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GN1, lemma-flatness-sheafification-refined: local flatness; the degree-zero derived scalar comparison is its K-flat application (proof in report)

proof.text: On each covering slice chart, evaluate the given isomorphism at its terminal object. Evaluation preserves the finite product, so M(U) is linearly equivalent to a finite power of R(U), hence is an algebraically flat module, including rank zero. Restrict a finite section relation to U and apply Mathlib Module.Flat.isTrivialRelation_of_sum_smul_eq_zero. These factorizations satisfy the independent-universe covering-sieve local relation criterion, proving site flatness.

The single complex M[0] is strictly bounded above by zero. Its degree zero term is flat by Step 1. Every other term is zero; evaluation makes all its section modules subsingleton, so the local relation criterion with zero auxiliary generators proves these terms flat. Apply the existing independent-coefficient bounded-above flat criterion to obtain the exact K-flat predicate in the statement.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat, for the degree-zero complex

proof.text: The supplied DerivedChangeOfRingsCochainModel fixes ordinary extension on objects and maps and carries the universal left-derived counit. Its computes clause makes that very counit invertible on the K-flat complex of Step 2. Composing with localization of the standard single-complex isomorphism gives the specified locallyFreeScalarComparison, with no assumption on flatness of the new ring.

Ordinary scalar extension commutes with slice restriction: the presheaves identify by identity on pure tensors, and the proved slice-sheafification comparison used in the localized tensor restriction module is invertible. Extension of the structure module is the new structure module, by the sectionwise B tensor_R R = B isomorphism and the module-sheafification counit. Abelian sheafification exists on the essentially small slice by coefficientSheafification. Choose the ordinary additive functor supplied by the existing cochain model on this slice. Additivity preserves finite products; applying this functor to any given rank-n chart and the unit isomorphism proves the same rank-n chart after extension. This uses neither a new universal pair nor a choice of arbitrary comparison map.

source.place: Section 03EK, tensor unit and finite sums; Tag 03EL, compatibility with slice restriction

proof.text: For an arbitrary module map M to N, apply naturality of the cochain counit to its single-complex map, followed by naturality of the isomorphism commuting an additive functor with a single complex. Functoriality of localization gives exactly the displayed square. No flatness of N is required.
